whatTheRunningBuildProves: The real final guardian encounter presents the Void Empress under corruption pressure.
The game routes the final point of damage through its real guardian restoration code.
The resulting running-build screen says Void Empress restored rather than defeated or destroyed.
The non-mutating result preview identifies the restored guardian as the Void Empress.
Both frames use a company-controlled invented state with no player or child identity.
captureBoundary: This is a staged two-frame QA comparison, not a continuous player journey. The camera safely freezes the full-health guardian, then stages the final point and uses the real damage, restoration, resident-return and result-screen code. It does not show the earlier combat or claim that a player performed the missing action between the two frames.

qualityIssues.observation: The background realm looks almost the same before and after restoration.
qualityIssues.impact: The pair proves a result label but does not visually prove that the player brought a living world back to health.
qualityIssues.handoff: Add a clearly visible post-restoration ecology, light, colour or Current change that remains after the guardian sequence.

qualityIssues.observation: The restored guardian disappears instead of remaining visible in a healed or allied form.
qualityIssues.impact: The emotional difference between destroying an enemy and restoring a wounded being is carried mostly by text.
qualityIssues.handoff: Show the Void Empress visibly stabilised, changed or choosing to withdraw before the result screen.

qualityIssues.observation: The two stills skip the player action between full corruption and the final restoration point.
qualityIssues.impact: The pair cannot prove the combat journey, player skill or a continuous cause-and-effect sequence.
qualityIssues.handoff: Create a continuous capture from a readable late-combat opening through restoration and its stable aftermath.

qualityIssues.observation: The restored frame is mostly a text result over the same dark playfield.
qualityIssues.impact: It is truthful supporting evidence but too visually quiet to lead a social post, trailer beat or homepage promise about changing worlds.
qualityIssues.handoff: Give the stable aftermath one strong visual reward that reads without explanatory copy.

allowedClaims: Mythical Void calls the final guardian outcome restoration.
The fight is against the corruption around the Void Empress.
The real game contains a Void Empress restored result state.
claimsNotAllowed: The pair shows a complete player battle.
The pair proves that the realm visibly changes after restoration.
The restored guardian visibly becomes an ally in these frames.
Every guardian and realm has the same restoration presentation.
The two frames are a continuous recording.

gameDevelopmentHandoff.requestedOutcome: Make restoration visibly different from removal by showing a stable healed guardian or realm change that a child can understand without reading a result label.
acceptanceChecks: The before and after frames are visibly different even with all words hidden.
The restored guardian or its positive effect remains visible long enough to understand.
The realm has a stable post-restoration visual state.
A continuous late-combat-to-aftermath capture can be completed without debug overlays or personal data.
A fresh phone capture passes independent visual review before public promotion.

nextCompanyAction: Keep GP-014 and GP-015 as internal supporting evidence. Do not use the pair as the lead proof that players visibly restore worlds. Recapture after the stable guardian or realm aftermath is strengthened.
